explanation: Maintain the ancestors whose right subtrees have not yet been entered. A smaller preorder value becomes the current node’s left child. Otherwise pop ancestors no larger than that value and attach the new node as the last popped ancestor’s right child.
spaceComplexity: O(h), where h is tree height
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The stack contains the ancestor path whose right branches remain eligible. A smaller next value must begin the current node’s left subtree. Otherwise the last popped ancestor is the nearest eligible parent whose right subtree contains the value, reproducing valid BST preorder.
walkthrough: For preorder [8,4,6,10,9], 4 becomes 8’s left child and 6 becomes 4’s right child. Popping past 8 attaches 10 on the right; 9 becomes 10’s left child. Level order is [8,4,10,null,6,9].
edgeCases: A monotone traversal can produce a skewed tree.
The stack avoids recursive construction on a chain.
